subject: Momentum briefing: Exec queue items & QBR asks
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: exec-distro@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Momentum briefing: Exec queue items & QBR asks

Team —

Quick weekly snapshot ahead of Monday's QBR prep: pulling out items that need exec visibility or decisions. I kept this tight (see tracker attached + sheet link). High-level: short wins, top risks that could move into the QBR agenda, and three asks where I need a decision or resource commit by EOD Tue.

Wins
- Hosted API latency rollout: 95p latency improved by ~12% after kernel tuning (metrics in attached PDF). On track for GA next sprint (owner: Infra Eng).
- New Dedicated on-boarding checklist deployed; first pilot (Acme Corp) completed warm-up successfully — no customer-facing incidents.

Top risks / blockers
- Private deployments onboarding: VPC edge cases causing delays in two pilot installs (Acme, CloudPartner). Need legal/sales runway for extended dev windows.
- SLA exception request from a strategic account (Acme) tied to data residency; procurement needs guidance on acceptable concessions.
- Capacity planning: upcoming burst demand for April 25 campaign—current reserved pool may under-provision unless we approve an interim burst pool.

Asks (priority & recommended owner) — decision requested by Tue EOD
1) Approve 2-week burst allocation (ops budget) for Apr 18–May 2 (owner: Karthik) — impact: prevents throttling for 3 enterprise customers.
2) Sign off on proposed SLA exception template for Acme pilot (owner: Laura) — small language concession on retention; legal ready to proceed with exec note.
3) Greenlight a small VPC engineering taskforce for the next 3 sprints to unblock private installs (owner: Soojin) — requires reassigning 1 senior eng and 1 infra PM.

Next steps: please review tracker (attached + sheet) and reply with accept/decline/hold for each ask so I can fold items into the QBR pack. If something needs a short sync, I can carve 15 mins after the all-hands today.

Attachments: QBR-ask-tracker.xlsx, q1-region-metrics.pdf

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Sr. Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: exec-distro@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Momentum briefing: Exec queue items & QBR asks

Thanks Rachel — solid summary. Quick clarifications: 

- SLA exception for Acme: can you paste the exact clause you're proposing to relax? Legal will need to see the redline before I sign off. I've added a short comment in the tracker (tab: legal-asks).
- VPC taskforce: what's the expected deliverable at the end of 3 sprints? If it's just a runbook + two resolved blockers, I'm inclined to approve repurposing the senior eng. If it's a larger refactor we should scope differently.

Also, can we add a short note in the QBR pack about the Hosted API latency improvement and attribute to the kernel tuning work — it's a nice engineering win to highlight.

Laura
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick responses — short status / next steps: 

1) SLA exception (Laura): I'll drop the redline into the tracker (legal-asks tab) by 12:30p PT. Laura, if that's acceptable, please mark approve in the sheet and I'll treat it as signed for the QBR pack.
2) Burst allocation (Karthik): I'll ping Infra now for the estimate and put the number in OPS-1984. If Infra confirms <25% extra GPUs, Karthik, consider this pre-approved pending your verbal sign-off.
3) VPC taskforce (Soojin): propose deliverables = (a) install runbook, (b) two pilot fixes (networking and KMS handoff), (c) rollout checklist. If that's aligned I'll coordinate reassignments.

I'll update the QBR pack by EOD Monday with these outcomes and a 1-slide summary for each item. If there are no objections, I'll mark the SLA and burst items on the QBR agenda as "executive decision needed" and we'll slot 5 mins each.

Thanks —
